visual_action: A young woman in a "I VOTE FOR democrats" t-shirt speaks to the camera at a large political event. She points to a light-up wristband she's wearing. The video cuts to a young man wearing multiple glowing wristbands. The final shots show a crowd of young people, including the man, waving their arms with glowing wristbands at the event. Banners for "HARRIS WALZ" and NCAA basketball championships are visible in the background.

on_screen_text.text: I feel like you're just here for the wristbands...
All you do all day is look for more wristbands

spoken_summary: A young woman playfully accuses a young man of being at the event just "for the wristbands" and "for the zipline". When he acts confused ("What?"), she repeats, "All you do all day is go on the zipline." Note: The on-screen captions differ from the audio, stating he is there to "look for more wristbands" rather than to "go on the zipline."
audio_music: The video starts with dialogue. A dramatic, low-pitched musical sting plays for comedic effect at ~2 seconds. At ~9 seconds, an upbeat, cinematic, orchestral track begins and continues to the end, creating a sense of excitement.
editing_pacing: The video is a short, edited skit. It uses cuts between speakers, a dramatic quick zoom-in on the young man for comedic effect, and ends with handheld footage of the crowd.
central_claim: Democratic political conventions are fun, energetic events that are exciting for young people.
intended_effect: To portray the Democratic Party as vibrant and appealing to young voters, and to generate excitement about its political events.
uncertainty_flags: The spoken dialogue differs from the on-screen text captions. The audio mentions a 'zipline', while the captions refer to 'wristbands'.
